Docs match what Callisto does today. Worktree wp-docs-reconcile-alpha, trail #374. Docs only, no changeset. Observe current behaviour with the real binary or source before writing; never invent behaviour. Fix: (1) docs/projects/OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md: remove obsolete empty-npm-token, Twine token-minting and execute-permission claims; say hosted OIDC success is not yet verified. (2) docs/specs/REQ-DX-V1.md: registry-binding coverage stated honestly (Cargo proven; npm/PyPI evidence via the repaired verify-real fixture); drop owner-open items that have shipped (inferred-only release PRs, canonical identity wire). (3) REQ-DX-V1 generated-workflow length: the owner chose to keep credential isolation, so replace the 40-line target with the actual criterion: credentials only in the execute job, workflow generated not hand-written; cite no line count. (4) The --format json stderr contract on failure: run failing commands with --format json, record what stderr actually contains, and make docs/cli, stability and release docs all state that one behaviour (keep the documented clap parsing exceptions). (5) README and publishing/config docs: distinguish packing with the workspace's own tool from uploading the npm tarball; keep native scoped-registry routing and the Yarn/Bun limit. (6) ROAD-TO-V1: replace the cargo-semver-checks idea for CLI/config/report surfaces with the existing schema goldens and snapshot tests that actually cover them, and add no new gate. Keep each edit short. Run just doc-check and just pre-push. Rules (from the lead session close-gap-for-alpha). Be fast and lean; GitHub CI runs the full suite, so don't duplicate it.
- Read AGENTS.md. Prefer a type or private constructor over a check; delete checks a type makes redundant; fix sibling call sites in the same PR.
- A check, preview, dry run or test must run on exactly the structure the real path executes (one shared graph or derivation, the real tool), never a projection, copy or re-implementation. When fixing a failing or flaky test, assert the measured behaviour still happens.
- No new traits, async or frameworks. No new error codes, JSON keys or flags without asking the lead.
- Work in a named worktree off fresh origin/main. Write the failing test first for behaviour changes.
- Local checks: `cargo test -p <touched crate>` and `just lint` (clippy) for the crates you touched; `just doc-check` if docs changed. Do not run local `just ci` or a fresh reviewer unless the lead asks; let GitHub CI do the full run.
- If you change a public signature in callisto-manifests or callisto-model, also run `just fuzz-check` (the fuzz crate is outside the workspace, so crate tests miss it).
- Run `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` only for new decision logic, not for merges, renames, docs, CI or tests; never commit mutants.out*.
- Merges and conflict resolutions: resolve, run the touched crate's tests, push. Nothing else.
- Changeset (`cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add ...`) only for user-visible changes, written for users.
- Signed commits, no session trailer. Merge the latest origin/main right before pushing (no rebase, no force-push). Push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm with git ls-remote, link the given trail, open with entire trail ci-pr.
- Trails are semantic outcomes shared by many PRs. Never change a trail's title or description (no `entire trail update` on it, no `entire trail create` to rename it). Put PR-specific text in the PR body with `gh pr edit <n> --body-file`. Link your branch to the trail the lead named; if your work does not fit that trail's outcome, ask the lead instead of linking it anyway.
- If CI fails, fix that failure only. If Entire raises findings, fix only wrong results, broken recovery, security issues or checks that cannot fail; report the rest to the lead.
- Report to the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) in under 5 lines: PR, sha, what you ran.
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5; never run two cargo builds in one worktree.

## worktree-wp-docs-reconcile-alpha
# OIDC trusted publishing

Plan, not behavior: nothing here ships before it is built, and the specs describe only what exists. Target: after v1. Delete this file when the work ships.

## Goal

Publish to npm, crates.io and PyPI with no long-lived registry secret in the repository. The CI job proves its identity with a short-lived GitHub OIDC token, and each registry accepts it for a package that names that repository and workflow as a trusted publisher.

## What each registry needs

| Registry | Trusted publisher is set up | The job must | Token reaches the tool by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npm | per package on npmjs.com: owner, repository, workflow file, optional environment | have `id-token: write`; run npm 11.5.1 or later (Node 24 ships it) | npm detects the OIDC environment itself and prefers it over a token. No secret |
| crates.io | per crate in its settings, after a first manual publish | have `id-token: write`; run `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action`, which exchanges the OIDC token for a short-lived crates.io token and revokes it when the job ends | the action's `token` output, passed to `cargo publish` as `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` |
| PyPI | per project on pypi.org: owner, repository, workflow file, optional environment | have `id-token: write`; mint an upload token through PyPI's OIDC exchange | PyPI documents the exchange as an implementation detail; the stable interfaces are `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` and `uv publish`. Twine takes the minted token as `TWINE_PASSWORD` with `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` |

A mismatch in owner, repository, workflow file or environment fails, and npm reports it as a misleading E404. Self-hosted runners are not supported by npm. crates.io blocks the `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run` triggers.

## Where Callisto stands

- Generated workflows already give `execute` `id-token: write` (for npm provenance), so the permission itself is not new there. Callisto's own release workflow does not: its policy check allows `id-token: write` only on `build-artifact`.
- Callisto passes the environment through to the tool and never strips `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` or `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`, so npm can see them. ADR 4 keeps authentication with the ecosystem tool, which fits: Callisto does not need to mint tokens.
- The generated action writes a temporary npm config with an `NPM_TOKEN` entry. With no token set that line may stop npm falling back to OIDC. Unverified.
- Twine is the PyPI uploader, and it cannot mint a token.

## Work

1. Decide the shape: a `callisto.toml` switch, or a generated-workflow option, for "this registry publishes by OIDC", so no secret input is expected for it.
2. npm: omit the token entry from the generated npm config when OIDC is chosen, and check the pnpm, yarn and bun publish paths. Only `npm publish` is documented to use OIDC, so each package manager must be tested.
3. crates.io: generate the auth-action step before `execute` and pass its output as `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`.
4. PyPI: mint the token in a generated step, or use `uv publish` where it is available; keep twine for the token path.
5. Diagnostics: an E163 hint for the npm E404 case that names the trusted-publisher fields to recheck.
6. Policy and docs: the release workflow policy check, `docs/publishing.md`, the init docs and the generated-workflow tests.

## Decisions for the owner

- Callisto's own workflow: allow `id-token: write` on `execute`? With OIDC there is no registry secret at all, which is the intent of "only `execute` gets registry secrets", but the policy check forbids the permission and changing it is the owner's call. A GitHub Environment stays out either way.
- One job holds the OIDC permission while the project's own build code runs (cargo build scripts during `cargo publish` verification, npm lifecycle scripts). That is also true of a long-lived token today, and a short-lived scoped token is strictly less exposed. Keeping the build in a separate job (the current build-artifact split) limits it further.

## Verification

Needs real packages, so it is owner-run. For each registry: configure a scratch package's trusted publisher, run a release from a scratch repository with no token set, and confirm the version appears and the tag and release are created. Include a deliberately wrong workflow name per registry and check the diagnostic. Local registries (Verdaccio, pypiserver, cargo-http-registry) cannot exercise OIDC, so they cover only the no-token configuration paths.

## Sources

- npm: https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers
- crates.io: https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action and https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/07/11/crates-io-development-update-2025-07
- PyPI: https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/using-a-publisher/

| crates.io | per crate in its settings, after a first manual publish | have `id-token: write`; run `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action`, which exchanges the OIDC token for a short-lived crates.io token and revokes it when the job ends | the action's `token` output, passed to `cargo publish` as `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` |
| PyPI | per project on pypi.org: owner, repository, workflow file, optional environment | have `id-token: write`; mint an upload token through PyPI's OIDC exchange | PyPI documents the exchange as an implementation detail; the stable interfaces are `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` and `uv publish`. Twine takes the minted token as `TWINE_PASSWORD` with `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` |

A mismatch in owner, repository, workflow file or environment fails, and npm reports it as a misleading E404. Self-hosted runners are not supported by npm. crates.io blocks the `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run` triggers.

## Where Callisto stands

- Generated workflows already give `execute` `id-token: write` (for npm provenance), so the permission itself is not new there. Callisto's own release workflow does not: its policy check allows `id-token: write` only on `build-artifact`.
- Callisto passes the environment through to the tool and never strips `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` or `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`, so npm can see them. ADR 4 keeps authentication with the ecosystem tool, which fits: Callisto does not need to mint tokens.
- The generated action writes a temporary npm config with an `NPM_TOKEN` entry. With no token set that line may stop npm falling back to OIDC. Unverified.
- Twine is the PyPI uploader, and it cannot mint a token.

## Work

1. Decide the shape: a `callisto.toml` switch, or a generated-workflow option, for "this registry publishes by OIDC", so no secret input is expected for it.
2. npm: omit the token entry from the generated npm config when OIDC is chosen, and check the pnpm, yarn and bun publish paths. Only `npm publish` is documented to use OIDC, so each package manager must be tested.
3. crates.io: generate the auth-action step before `execute` and pass its output as `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`.
4. PyPI: mint the token in a generated step, or use `uv publish` where it is available; keep twine for the token path.
5. Diagnostics: an E163 hint for the npm E404 case that names the trusted-publisher fields to recheck.
6. Policy and docs: the release workflow policy check, `docs/publishing.md`, the init docs and the generated-workflow tests.

## Decisions for the owner

- Callisto's own workflow: allow `id-token: write` on `execute`? With OIDC there is no registry secret at all, which is the intent of "only `execute` gets registry secrets", but the policy check forbids the permission and changing it is the owner's call. A GitHub Environment stays out either way.
- One job holds the OIDC permission while the project's own build code runs (cargo build scripts during `cargo publish` verification, npm lifecycle scripts). That is also true of a long-lived token today, and a short-lived scoped token is strictly less exposed. Keeping the build in a separate job (the current build-artifact split) limits it further.

## Verification

Needs real packages, so it is owner-run. For each registry: configure a scratch package's trusted publisher, run a release from a scratch repository with no token set, and confirm the version appears and the tag and release are created. Include a deliberately wrong workflow name per registry and check the diagnostic. Local registries (Verdaccio, pypiserver, cargo-http-registry) cannot exercise OIDC, so they cover only the no-token configuration paths.

name: Release

on: {push: {branches: [__BRANCH_FILTER__]}}

permissions: {}

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  version-pr:
    # After a release merge, decide reads the new tags: before execute pushes them it would re-infer released commits.
    needs: [package, execute]
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.package.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.package.outputs.release != 'true' || needs.execute.result == 'success')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: {contents: write, pull-requests: write}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false}
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@__COMMIT__ # callisto@__VERSION__
        with: {mode: version-pr, branch: __BRANCH__}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  # No registry credentials: project build code runs here, and the executing job publishes these exact files.
  package:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: {contents: read}
    outputs:
      release: ${{ steps.decision.outputs.release }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {ref: "${{ github.sha }}", fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false}
      # Content precondition, not release detection: `release plan` requires this commit to write its decision.
      - name: Check for a release decision
        id: decision
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release=false
          if git rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^ > /dev/null &&
            git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only --diff-filter=AM -r HEAD^ HEAD | grep -qxF .callisto/release-decision.json; then
            release=true
          fi
          echo "release=$release" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - if: steps.decision.outputs.release == 'true'
        uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@__COMMIT__ # callisto@__VERSION__
        with: {version: callisto@__VERSION__}
      - name: Plan the release
        id: plan
        if: steps.decision.outputs.release == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff="$RUNNER_TEMP/release-handoff"
          mkdir -p "$handoff"
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json \
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --out "$handoff/release-intent.json"
          {
            echo "has_python=$(jq '[.operations[].id | select(.role.kind == "registryPublish" and (.package | startswith("pypi/")))] | length > 0' "$handoff/release-intent.json")"
            echo "has_cargo=$(jq '[.operations[].id | select(.role.kind == "registryPublish" and (.package | startswith("cargo/")))] | length > 0' "$handoff/release-intent.json")"
            echo "has_npm=$(jq '[.operations[].id | select(.role.kind == "platformPublish" or (.role.kind == "registryPublish" and (.package | startswith("npm/"))))] | length > 0' "$handoff/release-intent.json")"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      __PACKAGE_STEPS__
      - if: steps.decision.outputs.release == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-handoff
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-handoff
          if-no-files-found: error

  execute:
    needs: package
    if: needs.package.outputs.release == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency: {group: callisto-release, cancel-in-progress: false}
    permissions: {contents: write, id-token: write}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {ref: "${{ github.sha }}", fetch-depth: 0} # zizmor: ignore[artipacked] tag push needs persisted credentials
      __TWINE_STEP__
      # The action's own setup would install the checkout's project-selected toolchains beside the credentials.
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@__COMMIT__ # callisto@__VERSION__
        with: {version: callisto@__VERSION__}
      # Downloads land under $RUNNER_TEMP: `release execute` requires a clean worktree.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2

# REQ-DX-V1: world-class release DX and correctness for v1

Stakeholder: Callisto owner (sole maintainer); users releasing Rust, npm (incl. napi-rs) and Python monorepos.

Status: open. The command surface and release machinery exist; [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) lists the verification and onboarding work that remains. Real local npm, Cargo and PyPI tests exist; the Cargo and PyPI ones drive the publisher directly and do not cover registry binding or observation.

Why: Callisto's release engine is rigorous but its surface is confusing and its setup is heavy. Goal: a new repo goes from `callisto init` to its first published release in under 10 minutes, with one obvious release command and no known correctness bugs.

## Decided by the owner

- The main verb is `release`. Flow: `add` → `version` → `release`.
- `callisto release` publishes every package whose version has no release yet: registry publish, tag, forge release. `--dry-run` previews it on any branch.
- User-facing commands shown in `--help`: init, add, status, version, release, pre, snapshot, completions. Plumbing stays callable but hidden.
- `add` keeps both modes: interactive wizard on a TTY, flags for automation, clear error with the needed flags when neither.
- Breaking changes are fine pre-1.0; no external users.
- Current implementation scope is Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm (including napi-rs) and Python/PyPI. Keep architecture room for Go and C#/.NET/NuGet without implementing those adapters now.
- Prefer canonical ecosystem-qualified references and deliberate legacy migration over collision-triggered identity magic. Release ownership, native distribution identity, version authority and effects are separate responsibilities; the detailed proposal is [the scoped model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- Do not build a universal package manager, build scheduler, cross-language inference engine or persisted execution journal. Native tools/CI own compilation, packing and authentication.

## Done when

- `callisto --help` lists exactly the 8 user commands; each has one plain-language line.
- `callisto release --dry-run` with no flags prints the full plan on any branch; `callisto release` with no flags performs it locally with credentials in the environment.
- The CI split (plan → build → execute across jobs) works through `release` flags or hidden subcommands, and callisto's own workflow uses them.
- `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag`, `filter-plan` are removed; one plan implementation serves preview and execution and includes every check listed above.
- Text output uses colour/tables on a TTY, plain text when piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, no schema versions in text; `status` shows cascaded bumps.
- A verified defect is fixed with regression coverage across affected siblings. CI runs the shipped runtime behavior; no shipped Cargo feature variants. The real local npm/Cargo/PyPI tests fail, not skip, under CI when a tool is missing, and production binding/observation paths are checked separately.
- `callisto init` detects ecosystems/packages, asks only intent (fixed vs independent; release artifacts if binaries exist), writes minimal config, and can write a GitHub workflow using `callisto-action` of <= 40 lines; a non-interactive mode exists.
- Supported fixtures cover separate native packages, and dual Cargo/npm outputs. Native dependency ranges/names, all affected lockfiles and built distribution metadata agree after versioning.
- A retry completes required missing effects without inventing a new version, even after tag creation or a partial Python/platform upload. Required outputs and shared public-announcement prerequisites are explicit; version/tag existence alone is not completion evidence.
- Generated workflows build/place only intended supported outputs and configure native authentication without registry secrets in plan, build, attest, package and pack jobs. This repo retains no GitHub Environment or separate reviewer gate; the reviewed merge remains the authorization.
- Fresh-repository runs measure init-to-first-publication against the existing under-ten-minute goal, including commit and credential steps. The supported/unsupported boundary is documented; no timing evidence is claimed until measured.

## Decisions still open

Authenticated private Python indexes and HTML-only indexes; npm dist-tag verification/promotion; universal registry checksum requirements; wrapper-specific bump severity; inferred-only/manual release commits under ADR 2; exact canonical-reference migration and release-owner wire representation. Record those choices before their implementation; do not make unstated preferences release gates.

Go major-qualified module paths/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are model examples, not promised runtime support or additional v1 gates.

# REQ-DX-V1: world-class release DX and correctness for v1

Stakeholder: Callisto owner (sole maintainer); users releasing Rust, npm (incl. napi-rs) and Python monorepos.

Status: open. The command surface and release machinery exist; [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) lists the verification and onboarding work that remains. Real local npm, Cargo and PyPI tests exist; the Cargo and PyPI ones drive the publisher directly and do not cover registry binding or observation.

Why: Callisto's release engine is rigorous but its surface is confusing and its setup is heavy. Goal: a new repo goes from `callisto init` to its first published release in under 10 minutes, with one obvious release command and no known correctness bugs.

## Decided by the owner

- The main verb is `release`. Flow: `add` → `version` → `release`.
- `callisto release` publishes every package whose version has no release yet: registry publish, tag, forge release. `--dry-run` previews it on any branch.
- User-facing commands shown in `--help`: init, add, status, version, release, pre, snapshot, completions. Plumbing stays callable but hidden.
- `add` keeps both modes: interactive wizard on a TTY, flags for automation, clear error with the needed flags when neither.
- Breaking changes are fine pre-1.0; no external users.
- Current implementation scope is Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm (including napi-rs) and Python/PyPI. Keep architecture room for Go and C#/.NET/NuGet without implementing those adapters now.
- Prefer canonical ecosystem-qualified references and deliberate legacy migration over collision-triggered identity magic. Release ownership, native distribution identity, version authority and effects are separate responsibilities; the detailed proposal is [the scoped model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- Do not build a universal package manager, build scheduler, cross-language inference engine or persisted execution journal. Native tools/CI own compilation, packing and authentication.

## Done when

- `callisto --help` lists exactly the 8 user commands; each has one plain-language line.
- `callisto release --dry-run` with no flags prints the full plan on any branch; `callisto release` with no flags performs it locally with credentials in the environment.
- The CI split (plan → build → execute across jobs) works through `release` flags or hidden subcommands, and callisto's own workflow uses them.
- `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag`, `filter-plan` are removed; one plan implementation serves preview and execution and includes every check listed above.
- Text output uses colour/tables on a TTY, plain text when piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, no schema versions in text; `status` shows cascaded bumps.
- A verified defect is fixed with regression coverage across affected siblings. CI runs the shipped runtime behavior; no shipped Cargo feature variants. The real local npm/Cargo/PyPI tests fail, not skip, under CI when a tool is missing, and production binding/observation paths are checked separately.
- `callisto init` detects ecosystems/packages, asks only intent (fixed vs independent; release artifacts if binaries exist), writes minimal config, and can write a GitHub workflow using `callisto-action` of <= 40 lines; a non-interactive mode exists.
- Supported fixtures cover separate native packages, and dual Cargo/npm outputs. Native dependency ranges/names, all affected lockfiles and built distribution metadata agree after versioning.
- A retry completes required missing effects without inventing a new version, even after tag creation or a partial Python/platform upload. Required outputs and shared public-announcement prerequisites are explicit; version/tag existence alone is not completion evidence.
- Generated workflows build/place only intended supported outputs and configure native authentication without registry secrets in plan, build, attest, package and pack jobs. This repo retains no GitHub Environment or separate reviewer gate; the reviewed merge remains the authorization.
- Fresh-repository runs measure init-to-first-publication against the existing under-ten-minute goal, including commit and credential steps. The supported/unsupported boundary is documented; no timing evidence is claimed until measured.

## Decisions still open

Authenticated private Python indexes and HTML-only indexes; npm dist-tag verification/promotion; universal registry checksum requirements; wrapper-specific bump severity; inferred-only/manual release commits under ADR 2; exact canonical-reference migration and release-owner wire representation. Record those choices before their implementation; do not make unstated preferences release gates.

Go major-qualified module paths/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are model examples, not promised runtime support or additional v1 gates.

README.md:19:Callisto turns per-package changesets into a version plan for Cargo, npm/pnpm, and Python/PyPI workspaces. It reads native manifests to decide which dependents need updates, then prepares the files and release operations for review.

README.md:32:| Package | Before | Planned change |
README.md:36:| Unrelated npm or Python package | Its current version | No bump just because it shares the repo |
README.md:38:The dependency requirement triggers the `service` bump; sharing a repo does not. Callisto does not infer arbitrary cross-language dependencies. Explicit version groups can couple packages that should move together.
README.md:41:- The release workflow uses native publishers and coordinates configured tags, GitHub releases, and assets. Package owners retain their hooks and credentials.
README.md:57:    release --> outputs(["Packages · tags · GitHub releases"])
README.md:73:- `callisto status` shows each package's planned bump. `status --check` exits 1 on an error-level diagnostic, so it works as a CI gate ([releasing](docs/releasing.md#pr-pre-flight-verification)).
README.md:76:- A mistyped package name gets up to three `did you mean` suggestions, and a wrong ecosystem is caught too ([errors](docs/errors.md)).
README.md:81:- `[[package]]` rules, matched by exact name or by glob, override per package: `release-trigger`, `publish-to`, `tag-template`, `previous-tag-templates` for renamed packages, `changelog` and `pre-major-inference` ([config](docs/config.md#package)).
README.md:87:- `release-trigger = "auto"` infers bumps from conventional commits. `pre-major-inference` softens them for `0.y` packages that have a prior release: `conservative` turns a major into a minor, and `conservative-feat` also turns a minor into a patch ([config](docs/config.md#package)).
README.md:94:- `callisto release` publishes each package whose current version has no tag, using the ecosystem's own tool (`cargo`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun` or Twine), then creates the tag and the GitHub release. `--dry-run` prints the plan first ([releasing](docs/releasing.md#local-release-callisto-release)).

Selecting one identity of a dual package releases every identity of that package, so the tag never waits on a subset of its publishes. A product's public release also waits for the tag, and so the registry publishes, of each other package whose asset it carries. Without a sealed file set (the local route, and a CI route whose manifest seals none) it is judged against the files the executing run builds, matched by name, and digests are compared only for files that run uploaded: a rebuild need not be byte-identical to an earlier attempt. A PyPI registry reads its simple index at `url` and uploads to `publish-url` when set, else `url`; both endpoints are part of the registry binding. Authenticated reads and HTML-only indexes are not supported.

Python distributions are built by `release build-python` and npm tarballs packed by `release pack-npm` (the workspace's own packer, so `workspace:` ranges are rewritten), each into a directory a later job downloads.
docs/architecture/release.md:54:- `release artifact-manifest --seal-python --seal-npm` records each file's name, size and sha256 in the manifest, so the run envelope's manifest digest covers them. `execute` verifies the bytes, then publishes exactly those files: `twine upload <files>` and `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`.
docs/architecture/release.md:55:- On the CI route, a plan with an npm or PyPI publish needs a manifest that seals each of them: none, or one that misses a publish, fails (E306) when the manifest is verified, before any effect, and again before the publish command, so the fallback is never a build or pack beside the credentials. The local route has no manifest: it packs or builds in a temporary directory with credentials withheld, then publishes the same way.
docs/architecture/release.md:56:- `prepack` and `prepare` run in the pack job; `prepublishOnly`, `publish` and `postpublish` do not run. The CI route publishes crates with `cargo publish --no-verify`: a credential-free job first runs `release package-cargo`, which compiles every crate of the release with one `cargo package --locked -p a -p b` call per owning Cargo workspace, run from that workspace's directory (one call per workspace because a lone crate cannot resolve an unpublished sibling of the same release, and a layout such as `native/Cargo.toml` with no root manifest has no workspace at the checkout root), and the job graph, with `execute` needing that job, is the record. The local route keeps cargo's own verification.
docs/architecture/release.md:62:- npm: copy existing user config to a mode-0600 temporary file, add an npmjs entry interpolating `NPM_TOKEN`, point `npm` at it, and remove it on exit. The original config is unchanged. `NPM_TOKEN` remains available for `.npmrc` interpolation. Custom registries use native configuration. Only `npm` publishes, whichever package manager packed the tarball, so no pnpm, yarn or bun auth is mapped, and a registry set only in a yarn workspace's `.yarnrc.yml` or a bun workspace's `bunfig.toml` is refused (E168) when the intent is derived, because `npm publish <tarball>` would not honor it.
docs/architecture/release.md:127:The tag/announcement barrier covers all required publications of a graph package: a package's tag waits for the registry publishes of every release identity it has (`OpIndex::tag_prerequisites`), so a dual Cargo/npm owner's one tag and public release follow both publishes, in no fixed ecosystem order. A dependency edge is not a barrier: it orders only the dependent's distribution in the declaring manifest's ecosystem (`link_publish_prerequisites`), so a dual owner's Cargo-only dependency holds its crate, not its npm package. Selecting one identity of a dual package releases every identity of that package, so the tag never waits on a subset of its publishes. A product's public release also waits for the tag, and so the registry publishes, of each other package whose asset it carries. An intent derived before either rule fails closed as stale and is rebuilt with `release plan`. See [the scoped design](polyglot-v1.md) for proposed ownership and future Go tag-publication semantics.
docs/architecture/release.md:135:Registry evidence currently confirms a version, with optional checksum/yank fields; it does not establish byte identity. npm publishes the sealed tarball only, and a manifest that seals an npm publish records one set per published npm package (a platform package under its own name), each exactly one file named as `npm pack` names it; the adapter rechecks the digest before `npm publish`, and a rerun adopts a version the registry already shows, so the tarball path is re-derived from the manifest each run and nothing is recorded. Python completion has two modes. Without a sealed file set (the local route, and a CI route whose manifest seals none) it is judged against the files the executing run builds, matched by name, and digests are compared only for files that run uploaded: a rebuild need not be byte-identical to an earlier attempt. With a sealed set, a build job (`release build-python`, no credentials) builds the files and `release artifact-manifest --seal-python` records each file's name, size and sha256 in the manifest, so the envelope's manifest digest covers them. `release execute` verifies the bytes, builds nothing, uploads those files, and treats any index file under a sealed name with another sha256 as an error (E307). The sealed sets are all or none per ecosystem and each belongs to a Python or npm publish of the intent; the manifest stays at schema version 1 because a manifest without sets is unchanged and an older reader rejects the new field. Artifact size/sha256 validation otherwise applies to declared GitHub assets. A PyPI registry reads its simple index at `url` and uploads to `publish-url` when set, else `url`; both endpoints are part of the registry binding. Authenticated reads and HTML-only indexes are not supported.

content.text:
Docs reconciled and pushed as PR #623 (trail #374), commit `9fa8d911d`, merged with origin/main. I did not check the signature after pushing. `entire trail ci-pr` created the PR, so nothing set its body.

1. **OIDC plan:** an empty or unset `NPM_TOKEN` or `PYPI_TOKEN` now reads as "configures nothing, so the tool falls back to OIDC". I removed the Twine token-minting claim. Callisto's own workflow allows `id-token` only on `attest`, not `build-artifact`, and I changed that line. It now says hosted OIDC success is not yet verified.
2. **REQ-DX-V1 (coverage and open items):** registry-binding coverage says Cargo is proven and npm/PyPI evidence comes from the `verify-real` fixture. Inferred-only release PRs and the canonical identity wire are gone from the owner-open list.
3. **REQ-DX-V1 (workflow length):** the 40-line target is replaced with "generated, not hand-written; credentials only in `execute`".
4. **`--format json` failures:** I ran failing commands with the real binary. Stdout is empty and stderr ends with one JSON error document. Exit is 1, or 2 for argument-parsing errors, which print clap usage text. Tool output, for example git's `fatal:` line, can come before the JSON on stderr. `stability.md` and the README now say this, and `cli.json` already did. The README and `stability.md` are the only docs that state this contract, since there is no `docs/cli`, so I edited those two.
5. **Packing vs upload:** the README and `how-callisto-works.md` now say the workspace manager packs the tarball but `npm publish <tarball>` uploads it. The README also keeps the scoped-registry routing and the Yarn/Bun limit. `publishing.md` already said this, so I left it unchanged.
6. **ROAD-TO-V1:** the `cargo-semver-checks` idea is replaced by a pointer to `schema_guard_test` and the snapshot tests, with no new gate. I did not check that the snapshots cover config formats.

`just doc-check` and `just pre-push` both exited 0. `pre-push` hit the sandbox network block on launch.moonrepo.app and passed once I allowed that host. I did not run `just ci`.
